Kevin Durant is absolutely not trying to hear any talk about cutting back his minutes 🗣️ 
During Houston Rockets media day, general manager Rafael Stone and head coach Ime Udoka made it very clear they want to lower Durant’s workload this season to keep him fresh.

But when asked about the team’s load management plan, KD gave a classic, unfiltered response.

He mentioned that both he and the team are simply better when he is actually out on the court.

That hooper mentality is exactly why Houston brought him in, but there is a massive debate brewing within the fanbase about how much he should actually play.

Last season, the Rockets leaned heavily on their stars.
 Amen Thompson led the entire league with 2,953 minutes played at just 23 years old.

Right behind him was Durant, who logged 2,840 minutes despite being in the later stages of his career.

He finished second in the entire league in total minutes played.

While that relentless competitive edge is what makes Durant an all-time great, the heavy regular-season mileage took a serious toll when it mattered most.

Durant’s postseason was derailed by injuries, limiting him to just one playoff game in Houston’s first-round series loss to the Lakers.

KD clearly isn’t thinking about slowing down, and he firmly believes he gives Houston its absolute best chance to win whenever he is on the floor.

But the front office knows they need him 100 percent healthy for a deep postseason run.

Do you think the Rockets should force Kevin Durant to accept a minutes restriction, or should they just let him hoop as much as he wants? 🤔
